summary:
Udmurtia has produced no division-specific transgender evidence in the available sources; a visitor to the republic stands under the national framework of Russia as it operates countrywide, and the UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression for Russia (June 2025) is the framework against which this division is assessed.

Consensual same-sex activity is not criminalised in Russia, but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned. Legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care were prohibited outright in 2023, when the law banning gender reassignment surgery and legal gender changes on official documents took effect; the UK Home Office note records that trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned the same year. The expanded 'propaganda' statute criminalises public expression that 'justifies' gender transition, so a visitor's own statements can constitute the offence.

Foreigners who violate these laws face arrest, up to 15 days' detention, and deportation. The US State Department advisory for Russia is Level 4, Do Not Travel, and carries warnings directed at LGBT travellers; official national government warnings likewise tell LGBT travellers what they risk.

The Supreme Court designated the 'international LGBT movement' an extremist organisation in November 2023. Human Rights Watch recorded 101 extremism-related convictions for participation in that movement or display of its symbols as of 30 June 2025, with defendants facing up to 12 years in prison. Human Rights Watch also documented 81 people found guilty in 98 cases since January 2024 of administrative offences under article 20.3 for displaying banned LGBT symbols, mostly on social media, and called on governments to offer safe haven to those fleeing Russia.

Between 2022 and 2024 at least 139 individuals were affected by anti-LGBT+ law enforcement. 'Gay propaganda' fines for individuals reach 400,000 rubles (about £3,600) or 15 days' detention. Meduza reported on 19 June 2025 that cases under the propaganda laws have grown eighteenfold over the past decade and that fines under those statutes brought more than 60 million rubles ($765,300) into the state budget over two years.

Enforcement following the designation was immediate. The Guardian reported on 17 January 2024 that within 48 hours of the Supreme Court ruling, masked police raided LGBTQ-friendly Moscow bars: about 100 patrons at one venue were ordered to face walls, searched and photographed, and at least two other venues were raided the same night. The Moscow Times (23 June 2025) reported that arrests, club raids and extremism charges defined LGBTQ+ life in Russia through 2025, with a St Petersburg queer woman describing herself as 'a second-class citizen' after the designation. In December 2024 the Associated Press reported that a Russian man detained on extremism-related charges over an LGBTQ+ travel agency was found dead in a pretrial detention facility.

Physical coercion against transgender people is documented. BBC Russian (27 July 2024) followed 'Ada', a transgender woman lured by relatives in summer 2021 to a conversion-therapy centre near Novosibirsk, where she was held for nine months and forced to take testosterone, pray and perform manual labour before escaping when police responded to a phone she had found.

The UK Home Office note affirms that LGBT+ people in Russia, including the autonomous republic of Chechnya, constitute a particular social group under the refugee convention, which sets the assessment standard for UK asylum claims.
tangentialFactors:
Neither source contains information specific to Udmurtia beyond the national framework, so the enforcement figures quoted here are national baselines rather than measurements of local practice. A visitor should expect the same statutes, penalties and designation to apply in this division as anywhere in Russia.

Two enforcement tracks run in parallel. Extremism charges carry prison terms of up to 12 years and account for the 101 convictions recorded by Human Rights Watch, while article 20.3 administrative offences for displaying banned symbols produced 81 convictions across 98 cases in roughly eighteen months. Most administrative cases arose from social media posting, which means conduct originating abroad or online can generate a domestic charge.

The scale of the propaganda regime has grown in volume as well as severity: eighteenfold growth in case filings over a decade, more than 60 million rubles collected in fines over two years, and individual fines running to 400,000 rubles. For a foreign national the operative risk is narrower but sharper, since penalties for visitors include detention and deportation rather than fines alone.

Comparative guidance is consistent across sources. The US State Department's highest-level advisory and the UK Home Office's asylum policy note both treat LGBT identity in Russia as a protection concern, and Human Rights Watch has asked third governments to accept those fleeing. The Guardian, The Moscow Times, the Associated Press and BBC Russian separately document raids, deaths in custody and coerced conversion, which indicates the risk is documented across several independent reporting streams rather than a single claim.
localsOnly:
Residents of Udmurtia live under the same national statutes as visitors, but with no possibility of exit from them: same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned, legal gender recognition is prohibited, and trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023. Gender-affirming surgery and changes of gender marker on official documents are unlawful.

Between 2022 and 2024 at least 139 individuals were affected by anti-LGBT+ law enforcement nationally, and the trend continued through 2025. Displaying LGBT symbols, largely through social media, has produced 81 administrative convictions in 98 cases since January 2024; participation in or affiliation with the designated movement is charged as extremism, with up to 12 years' imprisonment available and 101 convictions recorded by 30 June 2025.

Activists and open members of the community describe the effects directly. A St Petersburg queer woman told The Moscow Times she considered herself 'a second-class citizen' after the designation, and a man held on extremism charges over an LGBTQ+ travel agency died in a pretrial detention facility in December 2024. Forced conversion practice also continues: a transgender woman was held for nine months at a centre near Novosibirsk and subjected to testosterone injections, forced prayer and manual labour.

For residents considering departure, the UK Home Office recognises LGBT+ people in Russia, including the autonomous republic of Chechnya, as members of a particular social group under the refugee convention, and Human Rights Watch has urged governments to provide safe haven.
outOfScopeNotes:
No source in this inventory reports police practice, raids, prosecutions or healthcare access specific to Udmurtia. Whether enforcement in this division diverges from the national baseline, in either direction, is unresolved and not sourced here.

The inventory does not cover entry or visa rules for transgender travellers, the treatment of gender markers on foreign passports at Russian border control, airport screening practice, or access to documentation renewals while in the country. These are not addressed by the UK Home Office note, Human Rights Watch or the parent framework text, and remain not sourced.

Facilities access, including restrooms and single-sex spaces, and any protection available from local authorities in Udmurtia are likewise not covered. No hate-crime provision applying specifically to gender identity is documented in these sources.

Recognition of foreign marriages or foreign partner visas is not addressed, so the position of a visitor travelling with a spouse or partner is unresolved on this record. The currency of the cited guidance should also be weighed: the UK Home Office note is version 2.0 of June 2025 with its page updated 12 August 2026, while the Human Rights Watch figures are stated as of 30 June 2025.
